newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia gives Bre-X, Barrick deadline on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia gives Bre-X, Barrick deadline on Busang.

text.p: Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana has given Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp one month to settle with their local partners in the huge Busang gold find, according to a letter to the two companies.

In the letter sent on January 17 -- a copy of which was obtained by Reuters on Monday -- Sudjana said if Bre-X and Barrick failed to meet the deadline, all discussions between them and the government would be cancelled. The government would then have full right to manage Busang II and III.
The letter was addressed to Bre-X vice-chairman John Felderhof and Barrick chief executive officer and chairman, Peter Munk.
The letter was a reply to the joint submission made by Bre-X and Barrick dated December 16 outlining their agreement to jointly develop the richest ore area, contained in Busang II and Busang III.
Bre-X has estimated the Busang property in East Kalimantan province on Borneo contains at least 57 million ounces of gold.
Bre-X and Barrick have agreed to split the property 22.5 and 67.5 percent respectively, with the balance going to the Indonesian government.

"In one month, your companies should be able to settle a partnership agreement with your legal partners and then should with your respective partners report in writing to the government of Indonesia that you have reached an agreement without government intervention," the letter said.

"If in that one month that agreement mentioned is not achieved, then everything that had been discussed previously will be cancelled, and the government will have full right to further manage Busang II and III," it said.
